fields.value: A healthy, well-grown girl with high spirits; physical detail is otherwise limited.
Impulsive, loud, flirtatious, confident, pleasure-seeking, and largely untouched by reflection.
To pursue amusement, officers, attention, and the status of being married before her sisters.
Youngest of the five Bennet daughters, indulged by her mother and insufficiently checked by her father.
Fifteen for much of the novel; sixteen by the time of her marriage.
Embodies the family risk Elizabeth anticipates and triggers the late crisis through her elopement.
Youngest daughter of Mr and Mrs Bennet; especially associated with Catherine Bennet.
Longbourn, then Brighton and London; later follows Wickham’s postings.
Moves from unchecked flirtation to a socially repaired but financially unstable marriage, without gaining much self-knowledge.
Wickham: impulsive elopement and marriage. Mrs Bennet: indulgent ally. Elizabeth: sister who recognizes the danger but cannot prevent it.
